summary: Establish an optimal one-to-one correspondence between structural connectivity (SC) and functional connectivity (FC) diffusion-map gradients in zebrafish, by computing an all-pairs Pearson similarity matrix between the first 50 SC modes and the first 50 FC modes and then solving the assignment problem with the Hungarian algorithm on cost 1 - |r|.
use_when: Analyze optimal sc–fc gradient correspondence by hungarian matching
Generate optimal sc–fc gradient correspondence by hungarian matching outputs
avoid_when: Connectivity estimates are unsupported because sampling, preprocessing, or matrix alignment is inadequate
